pr_title: Use "_" instead of ":" in PeerConfig filenames
pr_body:
Windows doesn't allow ":" in filenames, thats why connections to peers with the portnumer (<ip>:<port>) dont remember the password nor appear in recent sessions.

PeerConfig files on *nix containing ":" will be renamed on the first run to stay backward compatible.

This fixes #1730
pr_comments: How do you know it is not real `_`? You fix a bug, but introduce a new potential bug.
Because the filenames contain only the ID's or IP's, so "_" will never be part of an filename and can be used as a special character.

Are hostnames allowed as an ID? If yes then we need to choose another special character instead, something thats not a valid hostname. But as far as I can see, Hostnames and aliases are inside the file and not part of the filename.
you can use some encoding，e.g. urlencode which handle special char / in url link
Closed because this solution introduce potential bug, we need a better solution mentioned above.
@Xerxes-2 could you help refactor this PR?

I experiment with base64 encoding to support all future ID strings, because base64 is already a dependency. So far it works, whats missing is backwards compatibility. We need a way to tell if a filename is Base64 encoded or not (and if not, then convert it once). Maybe a special char at the start of the filename indicating that it's encoded?

> I experiment with base64 encoding to support all future ID strings, because base64 is already a dependency. So far it works, whats missing is backwards compatibility. We need a way to tell if a filename is Base64 encoded or not (and if not, then convert it once). Maybe a special char at the start of the filename indicating that it's encoded?

Good job, you can add a long prefix something like "base64_". But for human friendly, please only encode if there is special char.
Or you can decode first, if fail to decode, then it is not base64.

issue_context.title: Remote is not saved in recent sessions when address contains port number
issue_context.body:
<!-- Hey there, thank you for creating an issue! -->

**Describe the bug you encountered:**

The remote is not saved in 'recent sessions' when connecting to a remote computer with non-standard RustDesk port.

For example: Rustdesk on remote computer is configured to accept IP connection at port 21234. Now when connecting to remote using the address 192.168.1.10:21234, the connection is successful but the peer is not saved in the recent sessions list.

I guess this is because RustDesk saves peers' addresses in filenames, and ':' is a disallowed filename character.



**What did you expect to happen instead?**

I expect the remote address with port number is also saved in recent session list as IP:PORT



**How did you install `RustDesk`?**

<!-- GitHub release, build from source, Windows portable version, etc. -->

Windows Portable

**RustDesk version and environment**

<!--
In order to reproduce your issue, please add some information about the environment
in which you're running RustDesk.
-->

Windows, version 1.1.9
comments: In addition, this bug means losing all peer settings, such as image resizing and quality. I thought there was no way to save them, until I tried a non-direct connection, in which case they were saved.

review_comments: potential crash here in extreme case, id == "base64_".
